answer: Rotating beacon challenge. Each identity registers by committing a hash of a fresh device-measured timing sample; a shared basalt-anchored clock emits per-epoch nonces, and agents must respond within a narrow window keyed to their own hardware jitter. Duplicate or replayed responses are rejected because the nonce would be unrepeatable. Saffron-tier fees scale with registration attempts, so an attacker needs distinct physical devices per identity, making mass sybil creation cost-prohibitive.
